content.title: About
content.content: Chicory beverage is a non‑alcoholic drink made from the dried roots of the chicory plant (Cichorium intybus). It has a mildly bitter, coffee‑like flavor and is often used as a caffeine‑free coffee substitute or a flavorful soft drink.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicory is cultivated in Europe, North America and Russia; roots are harvested in the autumn.
During World War II chicory became a popular coffee substitute in Europe due to coffee shortages.
High in inulin, the drink is naturally sweet without added sugar.
Chicory has a long history in traditional medicine for supporting digestion and liver health.
Dried chicory roots can be stored for up to two years in a dry, dark place.

items.title: Rich in inulin
items.content: Inulin is a prebiotic fiber that promotes the growth of beneficial gut bacteria and improves digestive health.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: The beverage contains no caffeine, making it suitable for people who avoid stimulants.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Chicory contains polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports liver function
items.content: Extracts of chicory root are traditionally used to aid liver detoxification and function.

items.title: May help regulate blood sugar
items.content: Inulin can slow glucose absorption, contributing to more stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to chicory.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Large amounts of inulin can cause gas, bloating, and diarrhea.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Chicory may enhance the effects of diuretics and blood‑sugar‑lowering drugs.

items.title: Pregnancy and lactation
items.content: Pregnant or nursing women should consult a healthcare professional before consuming.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicory beverage can be enjoyed hot or cold, diluting a concentrate with water or milk. It is often used as a base for coffee‑style drinks, smoothies, and dessert sauces. Sweeteners, spices (cinnamon, vanilla) or cream can be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried chicory roots in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Prepared beverage should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 3‑5 days.
